key_insight: Underwater C3-JEPA learns to predict how objects move and change during underwater salvage using only synchronized multi-view RGB cameras and vehicle control signals. It models contact-rich interactions in latent space, helping robots anticipate heavy-load behavior even without contact sensors.
problem_solved: The paper tackles the challenge of near-field underwater ROV salvage, where vehicle motion lags, object dynamics are hard to observe, and contact sensors are often unavailable. It aims to infer object-state evolution during complex interaction from visual input alone.
method: Encodes synchronized multi-camera RGB observations into latent representations that separate task-object information from contextual cues.
Conditions predictions on ROV control signals to model how the object state evolves under vehicle actions and hydrodynamic lag.
Learns a cross-view, object-centric predictive world model that forecasts future latent states during contact-rich underwater manipulation.
impact: This approach can improve planning and control for underwater robots performing salvage, inspection, and manipulation in hard-to-sense environments. For AI/ML practitioners, it shows how latent world models can handle multi-view, contact-heavy robotics tasks without relying on specialized tactile hardware.

paper_title: Underwater C3-JEPA: An Object-Centric Cross-View World Model for ROV Salvage
paper_authors: Yuncong Yang, Jinlong Li, Yulong Xue, Feng Wu, Chunwen Zhang
